newsitem.title: UK: Trade buying lifts LIFFE cocoa, but outlook murky.
newsitem.headline: Trade buying lifts LIFFE cocoa, but outlook murky.

text.p: Trade bids gave an early lift to cocoa prices on Friday after they dived to 18-month lows on Thursday, but traders said the market's prospects remained murky.
Origins had backed away and low prices attracted a reasonable degree of industry offtake at scale-down prices which secured a base for the market.
"We know it can't go too far down," said one trader after a 14-stg rise in the benchmark May contract to a midday level of 887 stg a tonne -- the highest for the session.
But the bounce did little to shake off the disappointment caused earlier this week when a raid by funds left the technical charts in shambles after a brief attempt to rally.
"I don't think we've seen the lows yet. There is more to do on the downside and the upside," said one, predicting a range of 870 and 910 for the May position.

Friday's rise was triggered by overnight gains in New York, where charts secured a constructive reversal, but London was vulnerable to a fresh selling bout down to 850 stg not that it reverted back to a long-term downtrend.
"The alacrity with which the rally has reversed suggests the downtrend here could well remain in place for some time yet," said Elli Gifford of Investment Research in a weekly report.
The midsession volume reached a healthy 4,103 lots but it included 400 Sept/March crossed at 43 stg and 600 March/May at 23 stg, traders said.
